limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
name: adder
notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here except the performance requirement is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. The one performance requirement (brief 160) says every prepared out-of-context point has a routed Vivado result; no Fmax or area bound is agreed. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.source: arith/adder/rtl/adder_carry_select.sv (g_first and g_sel blocks, two blocks)
requirements.text: A carry-select adder (a low block, and a high block computed for carry in 0 and 1 and selected by the low block's carry out) returns the same sum and carry out as plain addition, for every block widths m and k and every pair of operands. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Carry-select composition adds, for every width

item_views.title: Subtraction is addition of the complements

requirements.text: For every width n, a + ~b + ~bin on n bits equals a - b - bin modulo 2^n, and its carry out is 1 exactly when there is no borrow: the identity every variant's subtract path rests on. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Subtraction is addition of the complements, for every width
